regex: \bI hope this helps\b|\bOf course!|\bCertainly!|\bYou['’]re absolutely right\b|\bWould you like\b|\bis there anything else\b|\blet me know\b|\bmore detailed breakdown\b|\bhere is a\b
action: Delete assistant-chat leakage; rewrite the passage as in-story prose
notes: Chat correspondence pasted as content; may appear inside comments; chatbot advice given this way is often wrong. Scoped to narration: characters may legitimately say Of course!/Certainly!/let me know in dialogue; 'here is a' can occur innocently - review hits before rewriting.

regex: \bas of my last knowledge update\b|\bup to my last training update\b|\bmy (last )?(knowledge|training) (cutoff|update)\b|\bin the (provided|available) (sources|search results)\b|\bbased on available information\b
action: Delete the disclaimer; replace with concrete story fact or cut entirely
notes: Knowledge-cutoff/RAG-failure disclaimers; older fixed-cutoff models (GPT-3.5/4) emit these verbatim. Plain 'as of [date]' alone is NOT flagged here (legitimate usage exists); only model-self-reference and source-availability framings.

regex: \bwhile specific (details|information)( about [^,.;]{0,60})? (is|are|remains?) (limited|scarce)\b|\bnot widely (available|documented|disclosed)\b|\bmaintains? a low profile\b|\bkeeps? (his |her |their )?personal (details|life) private\b
action: Cut the speculation; invent or research the concrete detail instead
notes: Source-gap hedges: the model claims information is undocumented then speculates; the 'low profile'/'keeps personal details private' claims are themselves speculative and often fabricated. In fiction these signal the model writing around a gap instead of inventing scene detail.

action: Fill or delete the placeholder; never commit Mad-Libs blanks
notes: Unfilled phrasal-template blanks, placeholder dates (2025-XX-XX) and PASTE_/INSERT_ tokens. Caveat: comments in infoboxes are common (some templates auto-include them) and NOT an AI sign; only the specific 'Add ____ if available' wording is suspect - anything else is more likely human. Non-LLM preload templates also exist.

regex: \b(maintains?|maintained|maintaining) an? (active|strong) (social media|digital|online) presence\b|\bactive social media presence\b|\bstrong digital presence\b
action: Cut the canned presence claim; show the character actually using the platform
notes: This exact wording is idiosyncratically AI and relatively uncommon before ~2024; banned because fiction has no reason to produce it except essay drift.

regex: \bindependent coverage\b|\bmedia outlets?\b|\b(music|business|tech|trade) (outlets?|publications?)\b|\bprofiled in\b|\bwritten by a leading expert\b
action: Remove resume-style coverage claims; dramatize reputation through scene
notes: Canned notability-proving phrases echoing Wikipedia guideline wording (e.g. 'independent coverage'); more common in 2025+ AI tools; human press releases also cite clippings, so judge in context. In fiction these mark encyclopedic register drift.

regex: \b(stands|serves) as\b|\bis a (testament|reminder)\b|\ba (vital|significant|crucial|pivotal|key) (role|moment)\b|\b(underscores?|highlights?) (its|the|their) (importance|significance)\b|\breflects? broader\b|\bsymboliz(es|ing) (its )?(ongoing|enduring|lasting)\b|\bcontributing to the\b|\bsetting the stage for\b|\b(marking|shaping) the\b|\b(represents|marks) a shift\b|\bkey turning point\b|\bevolving landscape\b|\bfocal point\b|\bindelible mark\b|\bdeeply rooted\b
action: Cut the significance claim; replace with one specific concrete fact
notes: Puffs up importance of arbitrary aspects and ties them to broader trends (WP:AITREND), even for mundane subjects; may add hedging preambles before discussing importance anyway; in biology over-emphasizes ecosystem links and conservation status even when unknown. Distinct identifiable repertoire of stock framings.

action: Delete the trailing -ing analysis clause; end the sentence at the fact
notes: Superficial analysis bolted on as a sentence-final present-participle phrase about significance/recognition/impact; RAG chatbots may attach these claims to named sources regardless of what the sources say. The judgment call (is the analysis vacuous?) is left to the reviewer; this row only counts the syntactic frame.

action: Strip travel-brochure tone; restate neutrally with specifics
notes: Advertisement/travel-guide register; same stock phrases regardless of topic. Caveats: not all promotional writing is AI; older LLMs (GPT-4) are blatantly positive while newer ones are subtler and avoid superlatives like 'the best'; 'rich' and 'vibrant' are common English words - weigh density not single hits.

action: Name the actual source or cut the attribution; ground opinion in a character
notes: Weasel-worded attribution to vague authority; also exaggerates source quantity (one citation presented as 'several publications' or many 'scholars'). Caveat: 'such as' is only suspect before exhaustive-looking example lists; 'several sources/publications' only when few are actually cited.

regex: \bdespite (its|their) [^.;]{0,80}\bfaces? (several |numerous |many )?challenges\b|\bfaces? several challenges\b|\bdespite these challenges\b|\bchallenges and (legacy|future directions)\b|\bfuture (outlook|prospects)\b
action: Cut the outline-style closer; end the chapter on scene not summary
source_ref: wikipedia:Outline-like conclusions about challenges and future prospects
notes: Rigid formula: 'Despite its X faces challenges...' then a vaguely positive assessment or speculation about future initiatives, usually closing a rigid outline structure. Caveat: the sign is the formula itself, not any mention of challenges or challenging.

action: Use plain is/are/has instead of serves-as/features/offers constructions
notes: Replaces simple is/are with serves as / marks / represents and has with features/offers/boasts/maintains; observed in GPT and Gemini models; 'refers to' used to avoid 'is' in definitions. Caveat: do not confuse with past perfect ('has been featured'); single uses are normal English - density is the tell. Overlaps wp-ailegacy stands/serves-as alternates by design.

action: Replace AI-vocabulary words with plainer or more specific diction
notes: Merge with collation 2.33 AI vocabulary cluster. One or two hits are coincidence; many co-occurring hits in post-2022 text is one of the strongest AI tells. Era-dependent: delve peaked 2023-24 then dropped sharply in 2025; GPT-4o favored align with/fostering/showcasing; GPT-5 favors emphasizing/enhance/highlighting/showcasing. Context matters: key only as adjective, landscape/tapestry only as abstract nouns, underscore can be literal, highlight(s) can be a noun - regex cannot disambiguate, reviewer must.

action: Vary sentence openers; merge or recast the Additionally sentence
notes: Sentence-initial 'Additionally,' is the strongest single AIVOCAB marker; line-anchored sub-pattern of the vocabulary cluster (merge with collation 2.33).

action: Use sentence case in headings
notes: engine:title-case-headings - AI chatbots strongly tend to capitalize all main words in section headings.

action: Remove mechanical key-takeaways boldface
notes: engine:bold-density - excessive mechanical boldface inherited from readmes/fan wikis/how-tos/slide decks/listicles; often bolds every instance of a chosen phrase. Caveat: some newer models are instructed to avoid boldface overuse.

action: Convert inline-header bullet lists to prose
notes: engine:inline-header-list - vertical lists where each marker is followed by a bold inline header plus colon plus description; markers may be bullet char, hyphen, en dash, hash, emoji or explicit numbers; line breaks may be lost when pasted as bare text.

action: Reduce em-dash density; prefer commas/parentheses/colons where natural
notes: engine:emdash-density - MERGE with punctuation_format em-dash density row; do not double-count. LLMs use em dashes where humans use commas/parens/colons, in formulaic punched-up parallelisms. Caveats: only useful combined with other signs; humans use em dashes too; GPT-5.1 and some newer chatbots suppress them.

action: Replace unnecessary small tables with prose
notes: engine:table-in-prose - rare sign: small unnecessary tables that would read better as prose; in a fiction manuscript any data table mid-prose is suspect.

action: Normalize to one quote style across the manuscript
notes: engine:quote-style-inconsistency - the tell is INCONSISTENT mixing of curly and straight quotes/apostrophes in one text (ChatGPT/DeepSeek habit). IMPORTANT caveats: curly quotes alone prove nothing - they are standard in professional typesetting (Chicago style, newspapers), Word smart quotes, macOS/iOS autocorrect, LanguageTool; Gemini and Claude models typically do NOT use curly quotes; some fonts render the difference invisibly.

action: Fix heading hierarchy to not skip levels
notes: engine:skipped-heading-level - AI chatbots tend to skip level-2 headings and start at level 3; very unlikely in manually formatted text.

action: Delete horizontal rules before headings
notes: engine:thematic-break-before-heading - thematic break (----/***) immediately before each heading; common artifact of Markdown chatbot output.
